source_text: CONDITION ON DISCHARGE: Stable. ACTIVITY: As tolerated. DIET: Low-fat, low-salt, cardiac diet. DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS: Take medications regularly. PT, OT, speech therapist to evaluate and treat at Siskin Rehab Hospital. Continue Cipro for an additional two days for UTI. DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: Cipro 250 mg, one tablet p.o. b.i.d. for an additional two days. Aggrenox, one tablet p.o. b.i.d. Docusate sodium 100 mg, one cap p.o. b.i.d. Zocor 20 mg, one tablet p.o. at bedtime. Prevacid 30 mg p.o. once a day. FOLLOW UP: The patient needs to follow up with Rehabilitation Hospital after discharge. The patient can call the Clinic for a follow-up appointment or find a primary care physician.

annotation_notes: The self-contained passage was retained because it includes the patient's discharge condition, activity and dietary directions, rehabilitation plan, complete discharge medication list, and follow-up instructions. Medications remains the primary content type because the passage provides five explicit discharge medication regimens. Each medication regimen was retained as one fact containing its explicitly stated dose, form, route, frequency, duration, and indication when available. The two Cipro statements were merged because they describe the same unchanged regimen; both complete supporting statements were retained as source evidence. PT, OT, and speech therapy were separated because each rehabilitation service is independently checkable, while 'evaluate and treat' was retained as the stated plan for each service. The alternative options to call the Clinic or find a primary care physician were retained together because the source presents them as one either-or follow-up instruction. Stable condition at discharge was mapped to diagnosis as a clinical-status finding without a more specific approved type. No demographic facts were added because the passage contains no explicit demographic information.
